subject: Formal request: streaming first-byte vs full-token throughput SLA exception for Atlas AI POC
messages:
From: Jordan Lewis <jordan@atlasai.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA question for POC - streaming vs batch

Hi Rafael,

Quick question as we finalize the Atlas AI POC: our workload is a near-live summarization pipeline that uses streaming responses (clients display tokens as they arrive). For production we need clarity on two things so we can plan fallback and UX expectations:

- Time-to-first-byte (TTFB) expectations for streaming responses (p50/p95) vs synchronous completions.
- Sustained token-rate expectations (tokens/sec) once the stream is active — we expect multi-minute sessions with bursts.

Our engineering team has measured variable results in earlier tests. To move forward with the contract we need a short written exception that guarantees tighter TTFB on streaming for the Dedicated plan during the POC window, plus a minimum sustained token/sec floor or a documented fallback behavior when throughput drops.

Can you confirm if Redwood can provide an exception for the POC (4 weeks) that commits to p95 TTFB <= 450ms on streaming and a minimum of 1,000 tokens/sec sustained for streams longer than 60s? If not, what alternative SLO wording do you recommend that we can accept contractually?

Thanks — we are targeting an onboarding kickoff next Tuesday, so a quick confirmation would be appreciated.

— Jordan
Director of Product, Atlas AI

Attachments: poc-performance-metrics.csv (sample traces)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lewis <jordan@atlasai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA question for POC - streaming vs batch

Jordan — thanks for the note and the traces. High level: we absolutely understand the need to bound perceived latency for streaming UX. Below is a concise summary of how we typically differentiate streaming vs synchronous (non-streaming) endpoints and an initial proposal for a POC exception.

Typical platform expectations (hosted/Dedicated):
- Synchronous (sync) endpoints: target time-to-first-token (TTFT) p50 ~ 200–400ms for short-context requests, p95 depends on model & seq length (commonly <= 800ms). Sustained throughput for batch-style payloads is expressed as tokens/sec per allocation rather than per-request.
- Streaming endpoints: initial token emission (TTFT) has additional handshake/streaming setup that can add variance; for Dedicated we aim for TTFT p50 in the 180–350ms range and p95 under ~500–700ms depending on model and region. Stream token-rate is workload-dependent — we provide guidance (e.g., 800–2,500 tokens/sec per GPU-class) and recommend quantization/batching profiles to stabilize throughput.

Proposal for Atlas AI POC exception (requested window: 4 weeks):
- Commitment: p95 TTFT for streaming endpoints <= 450ms (measured at our ingress in us-west region) for sessions that fit the POC traffic profile you provided.
- Sustained throughput: minimum observed sustained token-rate of 1,000 tokens/sec for streams longer than 60s, subject to traffic shaping/MTU and model choice (we will run validation tests before the kickoff).
- Fallback: if observed token-rate drops below 1,000 tokens/sec for >30s we will activate a fallback policy (route to compatible lower-latency variant or notify client with a soft degradation header).

Next steps: I’m looping in Karthik and our ops lead (Marissa) to turn this into a formal exception document (SLA-exception form + signatures). Karthik/Marissa — can you confirm that the wording above is signable for a POC (4 weeks) and advise on any required legal/ops guardrails? I’ve attached the CSV from Atlas so you can see the sample traces.

If that sounds good to you Jordan, I’ll ask the team to prepare the short SLA-exception PDF and DocuSign link.

Best,
Rafa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: poc-performance-metrics.csv (echoed)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA question for POC - streaming vs batch

Rafa — thanks for drafting. A few edits from a sales/ops perspective before we present to the customer:

- Swap "TTFT" acronym to "time-to-first-byte (TTFB) / initial token emission" in the final doc to avoid client confusion.
- Call out measurement point: we should be explicit that p95 is measured at Redwood ingress (our edge) and that customer-side network variability is excluded.
- Add a line about a scheduled validation run (48–72h) pre-kickoff to confirm the 1,000 tokens/sec floor using Atlas traces and their chosen model & quantization level.
- Legal/ops note: include a clause that the exception applies only to the POC environment and is non-precedential for production/contracted Dedicated capacity pricing or long-term SLAs.

Marissa — can you take the draft and produce an "SLA Exception" PDF. If SRE needs to sign off on the measurement method, please flag them. Once ready I’ll send to Jordan with a DocuSign link and HubSpot deal note.

—Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lewis <jordan@atlasai.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: SLA Exception for Atlas AI POC — signature request

Hi Jordan — attaching the formal SLA Exception PDF for the 4-week POC (see attachment: sla-exception-form.pdf). Summary highlights:

- Measurement: p95 time-to-first-byte (initial token) <= 450ms measured at Redwood ingress (us-west) for streaming endpoints.
- Sustained throughput: validated minimum sustained token-rate 1,000 tokens/sec for stream sessions >60s after a validation run.
- Validation window: a 48–72 hour validation run will be scheduled prior to the POC kickoff to confirm the numbers using the traces you provided.
- Fallback: if post-validation performance falls below the floor for >30s, Redwood will route to a compatible variant and issue a customer-visible soft-degradation header; this does not trigger an SLA credit for the POC.
- Scope: applies only to the named POC (Atlas AI) and is non-precedential for production Dedicated contracts.

Please review and sign via DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/DocuSign/Signing/ATL-1987. Once signed, we will schedule the 48–72h validation window with your engineering leads and lock the kickoff time.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Operations (Redwood Inference)
